results.title: Improved usage limits in the dashboard | Modal Changelog
highlights:
Improved usage limits in the dashboard | Modal Changelog

August 27, 2026 

# Improved usage limits in the dashboard

We've refreshed the usage limits UI across the dashboard. Understanding threshold billing and usage limits has been a common source of confusion, so the new design uses consistent terminology and shows you clearly what your current limits are and how to change them.

Head to your workspace's Usage and Billing settings to take a look, and see the budgets guide for more on managing spend.

results.title: Workspaces can now set environment-specific budgets | Modal Changelog
highlights:
August 6, 2026 

# Workspaces can now set environment-specific budgets

Team and Enterprise Workspaces can now set Environment Budgets in addition to Workspace Budgets. Environment Budgets allow for a monthly cap of compute usage in a specific Environment.

Owners and Managers in these Workspaces can set, edit, or remove Environment Budgets in the Environments tab, and can see current cycle usage against each budget in the Usage and Billing tab.

More details in the docs.

results.title: Choose a region when creating a Proxy | Modal Changelog
highlights:
August 31, 2026 

# Choose a region when creating a Proxy

When creating a Proxy in the dashboard, you can now select the region it runs in. Previously, all Proxies ran in us-east; picking a region closer to your workloads reduces latency for traffic routed through the Proxy.

The region is set at creation time and can't be changed afterward. See the Proxy guide for more.

results.title: Opt in to V2 Sandboxes with an environment variable | Modal Changelog
highlights:
August 14, 2026 

# Opt in to V2 Sandboxes with an environment variable

Starting with version 1.5.4 of the Python SDK, you can switch to V2 Sandboxes without any code changes by setting `MODAL_SANDBOX_V2=1` in your environment.

V2 Sandboxes will become the default in the next release (1.6.0), at which point the same variable can be used to opt out. Our goal is that most users never need to know the difference between V1 and V2, or do any work to migrate. See the Python SDK changelog for details.

results.title: Exit Reasons chart for Sandboxes | Modal Changelog
highlights:
August 26, 2026 

# Exit Reasons chart for Sandboxes

The Exit Reasons chart is now available for any app that runs Sandboxes. You'll find it alongside the aggregate metrics charts on the app page.

The chart now also differentiates between OOM kills caused by hitting a Sandbox's memory limit and those triggered by the worker's memory manager, making it easier to tell whether you need to raise a limit or investigate host-level pressure.
